# definednet_host (Resource)

Manages a host record: the identity, addresses, role, and tags a machine gets when it enrolls. Use it for lighthouses, relays, and other hosts whose identity must exist before they boot; enroll fleets with a `definednet_join_key` instead, whose hosts stay outside Terraform.

Creating the host mints a single-use `enrollment_code`; pass it to the machine, for example through cloud-init user data, and dnclient redeems it to enroll as this host. Terraform does not track enrollment. The code dies at first use, so a rebuilt machine needs a new one: put whatever replaces the machine, such as its AMI ID, in `enrollment_code_triggers`, and the new code flows into the user data in the same apply (with `aws_instance`, set `user_data_replace_on_change = true`). A machine replaced for any other reason, such as `-replace`, a taint, a failed provision retried later, or a termination outside Terraform, reuses the stored code, which may be consumed or expired; change a trigger value in the same apply. Terraform destroys the old instance before it re-mints the code, so unblock a blocked host first. Re-enrolling keeps the record and its addresses but does not revoke the previous machine's certificate; run one machine per host. To give a rebuilt machine a new record instead, replace the host with `lifecycle { replace_triggered_by }` pointing at a resource upstream of the machine, such as a `terraform_data` holding the AMI ID; pointing at the machine itself is a cycle once it uses the code.

The API key needs the `hosts:create`, `hosts:read`, `hosts:update`, `hosts:delete`, and `hosts:enroll` scopes, plus `networks:read` when `ipv4_address` is omitted.

A replacement deletes the old host before creating the new one; with `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` the new host also needs a different `name`, and a different `ipv4_address` if one is set, because both are unique within the network.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "definednet_host" "lighthouse" {
  network_id       = definednet_network.main.id
  name             = "lighthouse-ams"
  role_id          = definednet_role.lighthouse.id
  is_lighthouse    = true
  ipv4_address     = cidrhost(definednet_network.main.ipv4_cidr, 10)
  static_addresses = ["203.0.113.10:4242", "lighthouse-ams.example.com:4242"]
  listen_port      = 4242
  tags             = ["site:ams"]

  config_overrides = [
    { key = "lighthouse.serve_dns", value = jsonencode(true) },
  ]

  # A new AMI means a new machine, and a machine enrolls only with an unused
  # code, so the change mints one. The host record and its addresses stay.
  enrollment_code_triggers = { ami = data.aws_ami.ubuntu.id }
}

resource "aws_instance" "lighthouse" {
  ami = data.aws_ami.ubuntu.id
  user_data = templatefile("${path.module}/cloud-init.yaml", {
    enrollment_code = definednet_host.lighthouse.enrollment_code
  })
  # Cloud-init runs only on first boot, so a new code needs a new instance.
  user_data_replace_on_change = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Host name, 1-255 characters, unique within the network. `any` is reserved.
- `network_id` (String) Network the host belongs to. Changing it replaces the host.

### Optional

- `config_overrides` (Attributes Set) Nebula config overrides for this host, which win over its tags' and network's. `value` is JSON, so use `jsonencode()`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config_overrides))
- `enrollment_code_lifetime_seconds` (Number) How long the next minted code stays redeemable, 60-604800 seconds. Omit for the API default of 86400 (one day). Changing it alone does not mint a new code.
- `enrollment_code_triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values whose change, including removing the map, mints a new `enrollment_code`, such as the machine's AMI ID. The host record itself is unchanged. On an existing host the values must be known at plan time, so the plan can say whether a code will be minted.
- `ipv4_address` (String) Overlay IPv4 address, inside the network's `ipv4_cidr`. Omit to have the API assign the next free address at creation, or none on a network without IPv4. A host without one, such as a host created before its network gained an `ipv4_cidr`, gets the configured address in place; changing an existing address replaces the host.
- `is_lighthouse` (Boolean) Whether the host is a lighthouse. A lighthouse needs `static_addresses` and a non-zero `listen_port`, and cannot also be a relay. Changing it replaces the host. Defaults to `false`.
- `is_relay` (Boolean) Whether the host is a relay. A relay needs a non-zero `listen_port`. Changing it replaces the host. Defaults to `false`.
- `listen_port` (Number) UDP port Nebula listens on, 0-65535. `0` picks a random port, which lighthouses and relays cannot use. Defaults to `0`.
- `role_id` (String) Role whose firewall rules apply to the host.
- `static_addresses` (Set of String) Public `ip:port` or `hostname:port` addresses other hosts reach this one at, at most 100. Nebula tries every address, so order carries no meaning and the API drops duplicates.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags in `key:value` form. Tags that do not exist yet are created by the API.

### Read-Only

- `enrollment_code` (String, Sensitive) Single-use code dnclient redeems to enroll a machine as this host, minted at creation and again whenever `enrollment_code_triggers` changes. The API never returns it afterwards, so it is null after import until the triggers change.
- `id` (String) Host ID, e.g. `host-24NVITAMHMJ6WU2OXDL63L4JCI`.
- `ip_addresses` (List of String) Every overlay address the host has, IPv4 first. Hosts on a network with an IPv6 prefix always get an IPv6 address.
- `is_blocked` (Boolean) Whether the host is blocked from the network. Blocking is managed outside Terraform; a blocked host cannot enroll or connect.

<a id="nestedatt--config_overrides"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config_overrides`

Required:

- `key` (String) Dotted nebula config key, e.g. `lighthouse.dns.host`.
- `value` (String) JSON-encoded value for the key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import definednet_host.lighthouse host-24NVITAMHMJ6WU2OXDL63L4JCI
```
